full/W: Fine-tuning a pretrained network changes its weight matrices. Take one, W, with d rows and k columns: here, a thousand by a thousand.
full/size: Training all of it means a million numbers to learn, and a million more to store for every task.
full/idea: LoRA freezes W, and learns only a change to it, written as a product of two thin matrices: B times A.
full/rank: B is d by r, and A is r by k. The rank, r, is small: here, four.
count/shape: B times A is d by r, times r by k. The inner r's match, and the product comes out d by k: exactly W's shape.
count/count: Count what is learned. B is a thousand by four: four thousand numbers. A is four by a thousand: four thousand more.
count/total: Together, eight thousand. That is r times d, plus r times k: r times d plus k, here four times two thousand.
count/frac: That is zero point eight percent of the million in W.
count/out: The layer now computes W x plus B A x. W gets no updates; only B and A learn.
merge/zero: B starts at zero, and A at random. So at the start, B A is zero, and the layer gives exactly what the pretrained one did.
merge/start: Training begins from the original model, and moves away from it only as B learns.
merge/merge: When training is done, add B A into W. The merged matrix has W's shape, so the layer runs exactly as fast as before.
merge/tasks: And each task keeps only its own B and A: eight thousand numbers instead of a million.
worked/ask: Now a W that is not square: two thousand rows by five hundred columns, with LoRA at rank four. How many numbers does it train?
worked/B: B takes W's rows, and r columns: two thousand by four. That is eight thousand numbers.
worked/A: A takes r rows, and W's columns: four by five hundred. That is two thousand more.
worked/sum: Together, ten thousand: four times two thousand five hundred, r times d plus k.
worked/pct: W holds two thousand times five hundred: a million numbers. So LoRA trains one percent of them.
